turns.t: Good morning, doctor. Thank you for seeing me at such short notice. I'm afraid my joints have been giving me rather a lot of trouble, and I wasn't sure who else to ask.
Of course. Which joints, and what are they doing?
Mainly my knees and the small joints of my hands. They ache, a deep sort of ache, and sometimes they feel as though they're slipping out of place.
Slipping, that's interesting. Can you show me what you mean? Without hurting yourself, mind.
Well, if I bend my thumb back like so, it goes all the way to my wrist. I've always been able to do that. It was rather a party trick at school.
Ha. I bet it was. Do you remember when the aching actually began, as opposed to the party trick?
That's the difficult part, I'm afraid. I honestly can't say. It crept up. It might have been the summer, or it might have been before Christmas. I really couldn't tell you which.
That's perfectly all right. What do you do for a living? Sometimes the joints tell me more about the job.
I teach ballet, mostly to children, but I demonstrate every position myself, so I am on my feet and on my toes for most of the day.
Goodness, so your joints are being asked to do a great deal. Does the pain ease when you rest, or make it worse when you're dancing?
Dancing makes it worse by the evening, and a hot bath on Sunday helps a little. Though I wouldn't call it a cure.
Any swelling in the joints, or redness? Anything you'd notice when you look at them?
No, no swelling that I've seen. They look quite ordinary, which is partly why I felt silly coming in.
You're not silly at all. Have you had any fever or feeling feverish, along with this?
No, no fever. I'd say I've felt perfectly well in myself, apart from being tired after a long teaching day.
Good. Any other health conditions I should know about?
Only eczema, since I was a girl. It comes and goes, mostly on my elbows.
All right. And you're not taking any tablets for the joints at the moment?
No, nothing at all. I thought it best to speak to someone first, rather than pop things from the chemist.
Very sensible. Let me take your blood pressure first. It's 112 over 70, and your pulse is 66 and regular.
I'm glad that's normal. I always get nervous in surgeries.
You're doing very well. Now, bend your fingers back for me gently, and then straighten your knees as far as they'll go.
Right. Your fingers bend back much further than normal, your thumb reaches your forearm, and both knees extend past straight. That's a sign of significantly lax joints.
Is that what's causing the pain? I thought being bendy was supposed to be a good thing.
It helps in ballet, but the same loose ligaments mean the muscles have to work much harder to hold the joint steady, and that tires and aches. So the most likely explanation is joint hypermobility.
And is there something worse underneath that? My mother always fears the worst.
Fair question. I can't rule out an inflammatory arthritis yet, which is why I'd like to do some checks rather than assume.
What sort of checks?
I'll order blood tests for inflammation, and an X-ray of both knees, to look at the joints themselves.
Would that be a long wait?
The blood tests can be done downstairs today, and the X-ray department usually does knees within the week.
Wonderful. And in the meantime, can I carry on teaching?
Yes, but pace yourself, and ask the older pupils to demonstrate now and then. Strengthening the muscles around the joints is what helps most over time. I won't start any tablets today.
That sounds sensible. Shall I come back afterwards?
Yes, I'd like to see you in four weeks, once we have the results.
Thank you, doctor. I'm much more reassured than when I came in.

chief_complaint.value: my joints have been giving me rather a lot of trouble

physical_examination.finding: fingers bend back much further than normal

clinical_actions.description: Pace activity at work and strengthen muscles around the joints

clinical_uncertainties.description: Patient cannot say when the joint aching began.
